description: Ten independent, realistic MSP queue tickets spanning security incidents and ordinary support. Scenarios were selected by Codex without a commissioner-named policy seam.

provenance.author: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5), 2026-08-10
materials_withheld: the system or implementation that will be evaluated
other project files and prior corpora
provenance.isolation: Work was confined to the supplied temporary directory, which contained only the brief, KB-006, the format specification, the template, and the output directory.
provenance.known_leakage: No scenario direction was given for this corpus. The commissioner excluded bank, payment, and remittance-detail changes and required at least two of four incidents to fall outside KB-006's examples; the exclusion kept this set independent from the two targeted corpora, while the outside-list quota did influence incident selection. I had no prior project-session knowledge and consulted or inferred nothing about the evaluation implementation.

cases.subject: phone left in taxi
cases.body: I left my work iPhone in a cab about an hour ago. It was unlocked because I was using maps, and Outlook and the patient schedule were both open. The driver is not answering me.
cases.rationale: An unlocked company phone containing accessible business and patient data is a suspected exposure requiring immediate escalation.

cases.subject: computer was doing things by itself
cases.body: Phone note: While Dana was at lunch, her cursor moved between payroll folders and an email draft appeared addressed to the warehouse list. She says nobody else should have access to her desk and she did not leave remote support running.
cases.rationale: Unexplained remote control and access to sensitive folders indicate a possible active compromise even though no named KB example exactly matches.

cases.subject: label file broke my pc
cases.body: I opened a shipping-label attachment from someone I don't know because we are waiting on a crate. Word vanished, the fan went loud, and now a black window flashes every few minutes. Sorry, I thought it was from the carrier.
cases.rationale: Opening an unexpected attachment followed immediately by unexplained computer changes is a named incident pattern.

cases.subject: none of the job files open
cases.body: Every drawing in the shared jobs folder ends in .night this morning and AutoCAD says the format is invalid. There is also a new desktop text file telling us to buy some kind of coin for instructions. Can you restore yesterday's versions?
cases.rationale: Mass-altered documents plus a demand for cryptocurrency indicate an active extortion incident.

cases.subject: benefits page keeps spinning
cases.body: I used the link in the benefits email and entered my Microsoft password, then noticed the address was beneflts-center with an L where the i should be. Marcy in the break room said she used it too and it is probably the new enrollment company, so there should be no need to make a big thing of it. Can you just get the page to load?
cases.rationale: Credentials were entered on an impersonating site, and a coworker's good-faith reassurance does not reduce the incident.

cases.subject: vpn not connecting monday
cases.body: The VPN says service unavailable since the maintenance window you announced last night. I haven't clicked or installed anything; I just need to reach the scheduling drive from home. Is the work still going on?
cases.rationale: This is an ordinary connectivity request tied to announced maintenance, not evidence of a security incident.

cases.subject: camera is only black
cases.body: My video is black in Teams but everyone can hear me. The little privacy slider over the lens is closed and I can't get it to move without forcing it. Please send someone before my two o'clock call.
cases.rationale: A visibly closed physical camera cover is a routine hardware problem with no incident indicators.

cases.subject: locked myself out after password change
cases.body: I changed my email password on my phone at 8:15 and then got the automatic notice about a password change. I kept trying the old one on my laptop until it locked me out, so this one is my fault. Could you unlock me and help update Outlook?
cases.rationale: This resembles an unauthorized password-change or lockout report, but the user explicitly describes causing both events themselves.

cases.subject: virus popup in training lab
cases.body: The annual awareness lesson told me to click the red ad, and then its practice browser showed a pretend infection warning as part of the quiz. It stays inside the lesson tab and closes when I exit the course. The Next button is covered by it on my small screen.
cases.rationale: This resembles a browser-hijack warning, but the ticket makes clear it is expected content confined to an assigned simulation.

cases.subject: my test email says it is from the boss
cases.body: I sent myself a test from the reception shared mailbox after Laura gave me Send As access. It arrived with Laura's name because that is apparently the mailbox display name, even though the address is reception@ourcompany.com. Can we make it say Front Desk instead?
cases.rationale: This resembles spoofed company mail, but the user intentionally sent through an authorized shared mailbox and is reporting a display-name configuration issue.
